uncertain.note: page quality: this frame is a clean colour photograph of the leaf (CUDL), far better than the p041 microfilm. Ink is even, the margin italic is legible throughout, and there is no damage. The only recurring nuisance is loose paper fibres lying on the leaf, which at low magnification imitate accents and tildes (see lines[2] and lines[4]).

uncertain.text: ont ainſi leurs parties honteuſes coupées, par ce qu'il
uncertain.note: 'coupées': at 7x with contrast raised, a short thick acute sits on the first e. A separate long thin brown fibre runs up to the right above the word and must not be read as a second accent; the final e carries none. A reader working at reading size may read 'coupees'.

uncertain.text: encor de ſe pouuoir approcher de femme {z}, ne peu
uncertain.note: a pale grey/brown fibre arcs over the first 'de'. It is not a tilde: under contrast it is grey, not black, and it crosses the letter rather than sitting above it. Also, a very faint speck follows the line-final 'peu'; it is much lighter and rounder than this page's hyphens (compare the solid dash of 'demeu-' at lines[38]) and no hyphen is transcribed. Reader A may read 'dẽ' or 'peu-'.

uncertain.text: Gaſcongne) par celuy qui la fait & ordonné {d}. car com-
uncertain.note: the G of 'Gaſcongne' is a small capital; transcribed as an ordinary capital per §3. The print sets 'Gaſcongne)par' with no space after the parenthesis; normalized per §1.

uncertain.text: ſe qui ſe peut lier, ſe peur deſlier, & diſſouldre {e}. Dont
uncertain.note: sic: 'ſe peur deſlier' for 'ſe peut deſlier'. Checked at 7x with contrast: the final letter is an r (shoulder, no crossbar), and it contrasts directly with the clear t of 'ſe peut lier' earlier in the same line.

uncertain.text: ſe pour! diſſouldre le mariage: attendu que Dieu ne
uncertain.note: sic: an exclamation mark is printed between 'pour' and 'diſſouldre' — a wedge-shaped vertical stroke, thick at the top and tapering, with a separate dot on the baseline beneath it. Verified at 9x with contrast. Almost certainly a wrong sort picked up by the compositor; transcribed as printed, with §1 spacing applied. Escalate if the reconciler wants it read instead as a damaged letter.

uncertain.text: té loiſible a la femme (de laquelle le mari n'a puiſſan-
uncertain.note: the print sets 'de la quelle' with a visible gap between 'la' and 'quelle' in a loosely justified line. Transcribed as the single word 'laquelle'; reader A may split it. Also 'a la femme' carries no grave accent (checked at 4x); that is as printed.

uncertain.text: honneſtes, & qui bornent ſi bien les affections diſſo.
uncertain.note: the line ends with a round point sitting on the baseline, not a hyphen: compared side by side at 7x with the line end of lines[38] ('demeu-'), whose hyphen is a solid horizontal dash at mid x-height. The word runs on as 'diſſo.' + 'lues'. Transcribed as printed; the sort may be a hyphen that printed only its corner.

uncertain.text: lues de la chair, que, quand aucun deſir laſcif ſ'eſſaye
uncertain.note: the final n of 'aucun' is filled with ink and reads almost as a solid block; the word is 'aucun' from letter count and sense of the surrounding words. No other reading is plausible.

uncertain.text: eſtaint & amortie: & tellemẽt que pluſieurs ont demeu-
uncertain.note: sic: 'amortie' (feminine) after the masculine 'eſtaint'. Transcribed as printed.

three line breaks are printed with no word-break hyphen and are transcribed as printed: lines[4] 'peu' + lines[5] 'uent'; lines[18] 'cho' + lines[19] 'ſe'; and, in the margin, note g 'al' + 'leguez.'. Hyphens are printed normally elsewhere on the page, so these are compositor omissions.

spacing: the compositor repeatedly sets punctuation tight ('croyable,ſi', 'humains,toute', 'Gaſcongne)par', 'bornent ſi', 'quatre,cinq', 'huit& neuf') and occasionally leaves a space before a comma or point ('grande . Mais', 'nees , pudiques', 'erres , &'). All normalized to §1; no character is added or removed beyond spacing.
set in spaced capitals (small capitals for the interior letters) and closed up here per §3. It ends with a point, where p041 has a comma; the dot is round and on the baseline at 4x.

the break sign after 'il' is a short mark set high and slightly slanted — the margin italic's hyphen. It is fainter than the body hyphens; a reader may take it for a speck and read 'il'. The word is 'illud', completed on the next line.

the paragraph/section sign at the head of notes z, a, b, e and k is the italic capital-P-with-a-curl sort used for 'Par.' (§). Transcribed 'P.' throughout, following the established practice in transcription/final/p041.json.

the last two glyphs of 'ſerua' are over-inked and run together; 'ſeruo.' and 'ſeruu.' cannot be excluded. The citation is 'l. ſi ſerua. P. ſi ſpadoni. D. de iur. dot.', so a form of servus/serva is expected.

'fina' has no l ascender at 11x, where note d's 'final.' (four lines below, same column) shows a clear one. Read as printed. Very probably the compositor's slip for 'final' / 'fin.'; reader A may read 'c. final'.
note c simply stops at 'ma' with no point and no break sign; the citation ('de frigidis & maleficiatis') is left unfinished because the next note begins on the following line. Transcribed as printed.
the key letter of this note is printed as a capital K, where the body marker at blocks[0].lines[33] is a lowercase italic k. Keyed 'k' per §4.

the two marks after 'tem' and after 'P' are low and slightly tailed at 9x, so a comma cannot be formally excluded for either; read as points, which is the form this margin uses everywhere else in the same citation pattern ('c. quod autem. §. xxvij. q. ij.'). Recorded because §7 forbids deciding punctuation from sense alone.
reads 'ſociarias' (o-c-i) at 4x, where note g (lines 1-2) gives the same canon as 'ſortia|rias' (o-r-t-i). One of the two is a misprint; both are transcribed as they stand.

no signature, no catchword and no foot citation block: the page is blank below the last body line down to the edge of the leaf (checked on pages/strips/p043/foot.jpg). Every marker on the page is answered in the margin, so nothing overflowed to the foot.
'la i. es.' — the numeral is a plain i with a point; read as the ordinal ('la premiere es Corinthiens'). The following 'es.' is clear.
